item.title: Phulpati Dashain Messages: Nepal PM and President urge unity; Shah recalls Bhotekoshi floods
item.description: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah and President Ramchandra Paudel share heartfelt festive wishes for Bada Dashain, underlining family cohesion and social harmony. In light of recent floods, Shah expresses sympathy for those affected while advocating for recovery efforts. Paudel notes the festival’s significance in fostering goodwill and cultural richness across Nepal’s communities, urging citizens to cherish their traditions and unite in celebration despite struggles.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Over 1,000 residents oppose A$15bn data centre planned near Wagga Wagga
item.description: A proposed A$15 billion data-centre campus near Wagga Wagga has ignited a heated community conversation. Local residents express concerns about the impact on agricultural land, increased energy requirements, and ripple effects on the environment. Conversely, advocates highlight the prospects of enhanced economic growth and job opportunities for the area. The state government will assess these implications before making a final decision, with residents urging thorough evaluations to address their worries.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Violent Albania Protests Escalate: Student movement confronts Edi Rama; hundreds detained, dozens injured
item.description: In Tirana, a large assembly of students is rallying for Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation, citing rampant corruption. Tensions escalated into violent confrontations with riot police, resulting in several injuries. The protests highlight widespread dissatisfaction in Albania linked to job scarcity and corruption, aligning with similar movements across Europe regarding public services and living expenses.

item.title: Tear Gas At France Protests: Police clash with crowds over rising costs; authorities fear unrest
item.description: Nationwide protests erupted in France against soaring living costs and a decline in social welfare. Major cities like Paris and Marseille witnessed intense confrontations between law enforcement and demonstrators as tensions flared. With thousands taking to the streets, authorities are wary of possible chaos. Originating in northern suburbs where public service grievances peaked, both governmental and opposition factions are blaming each other for the unrest.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Texas landlord kept couple’s $2,600 deposit and sued; tenants won damages as appeal mostly failed
item.description: In a recent Texas court case, a landlord's attempt to retain a couple's security deposit, along with demands for extra payments post-move-out, was contested. The tenants triumphed, though the court adjusted some damage estimates. Texas statutes mandate landlords to avoid withholding deposits for usual wear and tear and to furnish detailed deductions. The ruling underlines the necessity for landlords to adhere to security deposit regulations strictly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Reese Witherspoon moves to buy back Hello Sunshine after 2021’s $900 million deal
item.description: Reese Witherspoon's recent collaboration with Mediawan to reacquire Hello Sunshine from Candle Media marks a pivotal moment in the entertainment sector. This transaction underscores rising transformations in valuation methods, as Hello Sunshine had previously commanded a valuation surpassing $900 million. With an ambition to enhance its narrative quality and global presence, Witherspoon is dedicated to guiding the company's creative trajectory and upcoming projects.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Pope Leo XIV to be discharged from hospital after successful lung cancer surgery today
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is set to leave the hospital after a successful lung cancer surgery, demonstrating commendable recovery progress. He engaged positively with his senior aides, expressing heartfelt gratitude towards the medical team for their dedicated care. As doctors await crucial test results to plan further treatment, the pontiff's upcoming trip to Latin America from November 6 to 17 highlights his determination to fulfill his commitments.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: ‘JD wanted to chat with us real quick’: How Trump’s press secretary was fired mid-interview
item.description: Katie Zacharia's brief tenure as White House press secretary ended abruptly after just five days due to a rocky start marked by an underwhelming briefing and questions regarding her qualifications. Despite Donald Trump's warning to reconsider the role, she was determined to fulfill her duties to the president and the nation. Her departure leaves the press office in limbo, especially with midterm elections approaching.
item.dc:creator: Aashish Vashistha

item.title: Islandwide Power Outage: Sri Lanka hit by multi-hour blackout; hydropower failure probed
item.description: Sri Lanka faced a significant power outage that affected the entire island for over three hours. Essential services such as water supply, internet, and mobile connectivity were disrupted during this time. Authorities are investigating the cause, with a potential failure at a hydropower station being considered. Citizens were warned to conserve water due to the impact on supplies from power cuts.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Mother tried to protect daughter's property rights in 1987; 39 years later, court rules against her
item.description: A property transfer made by a Queens mother in 1987 led to a legal dispute nearly four decades later. Mary Mangiaracina had tried to secure lifetime rights to the Ridgewood property for herself and her daughter. However, after the property was sold to new owners, her daughter challenged the sale-related ownership claims in court. In April 2026, a New York appeals court ruled that the daughter had never legally received those lifetime rights.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Brad Paisley and wife pledged $1 million for a free grocery store in 2024; it opened in 2026
item.description: Brad Paisley and Kimberly Williams-Paisley have expanded their philanthropic efforts by launching a second location of The Store, a nonprofit grocery aimed at combating food insecurity in Nashville. Following their first store's success in 2020, which garnered over 3,100 dedicated volunteers, the couple has invested $1 million into this new initiative to ensure families receive dignified access to food choices and additional resources.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Retirement Fuels Bushland Restoration: Ken and Jill revive 970ha bush; older Australians follow
item.description: In their eighties, Ken and Jill Hooper have become dedicated stewards of bushland in Australia, showcasing an inspiring commitment to conservation post-retirement. Over the last twenty years, after acquiring properties in Victoria and New South Wales, they focus on enhancing biodiversity and curbing invasive species to safeguard native wildlife. Their work reflects a significant trend of older Australians contributing to community conservation, aiming to foster a legacy for future generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 10 charred to death in fire at seaside resort in Bangladesh
item.description: At least 10 people were killed and nine injured after a fire gutted a three-storey seaside resort in Bangladesh’s Cox’s Bazar district early Saturday, The Express Tribune reported. The blaze broke out around 6.30am at TUPTUP Resto and Resort, built mainly of bamboo and wood. The cause remains unknown, while several people’s whereabouts were unclear. Injured victims were taken to hospital.
item.dc:creator: Aastha Jha

item.title: US ranchers win pipeline compensation fight but face $300,000 legal bill, Supreme Court to hear case
item.description: A group of North Dakota ranchers who spent nearly $300,000 fighting a pipeline company over land compensation have taken their dispute over legal expenses to the US Supreme Court. Although they reached a settlement, an appeals court ruled that the company need not cover their legal costs. The Supreme Court will hear the case on November 9.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Stephen King’s $3 million pledge helped transform hometown library into a $9.6 million project
item.description: Stephen and Tabitha King have committed $3 million to the Bangor Public Library renovation, provided that $6 million is raised through community efforts. Thanks to local support and a municipal bond, the library hit its $9 million target, kickstarting essential upgrades like roof repairs and improved community spaces, honoring both its historical significance and modern audience requirements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Forgotten John Constable Painting: $37 buy authenticated at $315,000; other 2024 finds hidden in plain sight
item.description: Hidden away in a cupboard for years, a painting believed to be by John Constable was recently found and has skyrocketed in value from its auction price of $37 to an astounding $315,000. This extraordinary revelation joins the ranks of remarkable discoveries, like a rare Lego mask and a Victorian brooch, which emphasize that ordinary objects can possess extraordinary worth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Snakes Found Inside Airport: Venomous western browns spotted in terminal; experts explain heat-driven visits
item.description: As summer approaches, Alice Springs Airport is preparing for an influx of snake sightings, with multiple reports emerging from terminal areas. In response, the airport management has put in place monitoring systems and hired professionals for safe snake removal. Travelers are encouraged to remain alert and immediately report any sightings to airport personnel, emphasizing safety first in this reptilian season.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
